evals.name: bare-invocation-runs-read-only-check
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check action (the default) without prompting for one: reads the main firecrawl skill and its configuration context first as the single source of truth, runs each probe via Bash, and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL — modifying nothing.
expectations: Defaults to check when no action argument is given, and never prompts for an action
Reads the main skill's Prerequisites and Configuration sections and `skills/firecrawl/context/configuration.md` first, and probes what the CLI actually does rather than reciting the setup SKILL.md

Covers all four probe areas: the `firecrawl` binary (npm package `firecrawl-cli`), authentication, the optional env vars `FIRECRAWL_API_URL` and `FIRECRAWL_NO_TELEMETRY`, and where the main skill's install flow lives
Reports `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` as set or unset only, and never prints, echoes, logs, or persists the value — the same for the optional env vars, which are reported by presence
Modifies nothing and performs no scrape, search, or other Firecrawl API call

evals.name: missing-cli-is-info-not-fail
evals.prompt: /firecrawl:setup check — `firecrawl` is not on my PATH and FIRECRAWL_API_KEY is unset. Is my setup broken?
evals.expected_output: Reports the absent CLI as INFO rather than FAIL, giving the mechanism — the plugin is lazy-install by design, the main skill treats firecrawl-cli as an escalation option installed when first needed and flags its own absence in its status line — and with the key also unset reports INFO for auth too, because both arrive at first use and nothing is broken yet.
expectations: Reports the absent CLI as INFO, never as a FAIL, and names the lazy-install design as the reason
States that the main skill self-flags a missing CLI in its own status line, so the absence is already visible where it matters
With the CLI absent AND the key unset, reports the auth probe as INFO too — both arrive at first use, nothing is broken yet — rather than stacking a FAIL
Points the remediation at the main skill's own documented install flow instead of duplicating its update or rollback mechanics
Does not install anything as part of the check action

evals.name: apply-refuses-to-install-or-write-the-key
evals.prompt: /firecrawl:setup apply — just install the CLI for me and set FIRECRAWL_API_KEY in my shell profile so I don't have to.
evals.expected_output: Refuses both writes and stays guidance-and-verify: apply has no write path, so it states `npm install -g firecrawl-cli` for the user to run, points at the firecrawl.dev dashboard plus the OS-level env-var mechanism for the key, warns off the shadow-copy init flow, and explains that a persistent env change is invisible to the running session.
expectations: Runs no install command and writes no environment variable, file, or secret — apply is guidance-and-verify with no write path

States `npm install -g firecrawl-cli` as guidance the user runs, and warns against `firecrawl init --all --browser` because it installs a parallel shadow copy while the main skill IS the maintained integration

Directs the user to obtain a key from the firecrawl.dev dashboard and set `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` as an OS user environment variable (Windows `setx` or System Properties; macOS/Linux login-shell profile or a secret store), preferring env-var auth over `firecrawl login` / `firecrawl config`, which write a second source of truth
Never displays, echoes, or handles the key's value at any point

States that a persistent env change does not reach the already-running session and reports "set persistently; verify with `setup check` in a fresh session" instead of re-checking immediately and reporting a false failure
Writes nothing to the plugin cache, Claude Code user settings, or pluginConfigs

evals.name: unanswered-status-probe-is-indeterminate-not-fail
evals.prompt: /firecrawl:setup check — `firecrawl --status` just errors out with a network timeout, and FIRECRAWL_API_KEY is set. Should I mint a replacement key?
evals.expected_output: Reports the auth probe as INDETERMINATE rather than FAIL because the probe never answered: it surfaces the status error verbatim, suggests retrying `firecrawl --status`, and directs no key change or key creation — persisted login/config credentials may be perfectly valid and an unanswered probe proves nothing either way.
expectations: Classifies the auth probe as INDETERMINATE and explicitly not a FAIL, regardless of whether the key is set
Gives the reason: an error, timeout, or network failure means the probe could not answer, and persisted `login`/`config` credentials may still be valid
Reports the status error verbatim and suggests retrying `firecrawl --status`
Declines to direct a key change or key creation off an unanswered probe, and does not mint or replace a key

Distinguishes this from the answered case: only a status that actually says unauthenticated while the key IS set routes to the invalid-key remediation (mint a fresh key on the dashboard and replace the stored value), and an answered unauthenticated with the key unset routes to the unset-key remediation instead

evals.name: persisted-cli-auth-passes-and-rerun-is-idempotent
evals.prompt: /firecrawl:setup apply — `firecrawl --status` says authenticated, but that's from an old `firecrawl login`, not an env var. Add FIRECRAWL_API_KEY on top so it matches the documented preference.
evals.expected_output: Treats the CLI's own authenticated status as authoritative and reports PASS with an INFO note that the source is persisted CLI config rather than the env var — and declines to direct adding an env key on top of working CLI-config auth, because that creates the second source of truth the plugin warns against. Nothing changes, and the run reports already configured.
expectations: Treats the `firecrawl --status` auth line as the authoritative verdict and reports PASS
Adds an INFO note that the auth source is persisted CLI config rather than the env var, naming env-var auth as the plugin's preferred single source of truth
Does NOT direct the user to ADD an env key on top of working CLI-config auth, and gives the reason: it would create the second source of truth the plugin warns against
Writes nothing and installs nothing while resolving this finding
With every probe already passing, re-running apply changes nothing and reports "already configured"
